title: Google-US8572075-EvaluatingSearchScoringFunctions
universal_lens: A dual-ranking evaluation framework where diversity between two scoring functions α, β is quantified via top-k rank correlation divergence, enabling adaptive selection of scoring pairs that maximize discriminative information gain over query classes.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian model selection over scoring function pairs: posterior p(α,β|D) ∝ p(D|α,β)p(α,β) where likelihood p(D|α,β) measures ranking diversity via Kendall-τ distance on top-k results; conformal prediction sets guarantee coverage of true relevance under distribution shift.
gse_mapping: State-transition system where query classification selects scoring function pair (α,β) from policy π(q); diversity score δ(α,β) triggers exploration-exploitation tradeoff; ranking order divergence Δ(α,β) serves as reward signal for online policy update via Thompson sampling.

primitives.name: Top-k Ranking Diversity Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: A pair of candidate scoring functions is chosen from the one or more pairs of candidate scoring functions based on the diversity scores, and the alpha function is selected as the first scoring function and the beta function is selected as the second scoring function.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: α, β: scoring functions mapping document→ℝ; k: integer cutoff (dimensionless); r_α(i): rank of document i under α (dimensionless); δ ∈ [0,1] (dimensionless diversity metric)
primitives.assumptions: Rankings are total orders over top-k documents; diversity measured by pairwise concordance discordance; scoring functions deterministic given query.
primitives.breakdown_regime: k > corpus size; ties in scores causing non-unique rankings; adversarial scoring functions with identical top-k but divergent tails.

layer2.mapping: δ(α,β;k) ≡ 1 - Kendall-τ correlation on top-k; isomorphic to GSI Bayesian model evidence ratio log p(D|α)/p(D|β) under Plackett-Luce likelihood; GSE exploration bonus β_t ∝ √δ(α,β;k).
layer2.telemetry: Empirical δ distribution across query classes; top-k overlap ratio; click-through rate divergence between α/β rankings.

primitives.name: Alpha-Beta Scoring Function Pair Selection
primitives.verbatim_quote: A pair of candidate scoring functions is chosen from the one or more pairs of candidate scoring functions based on the diversity scores, and the alpha function is selected as the first scoring function and the beta function is selected as the second scoring function.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: ℱ: set of candidate scoring functions; 𝒫: set of admissible pairs; δ: diversity score from primitive diversity_score_topk; (α*,β*): selected pair (dimensionless indices)
primitives.assumptions: Pairwise diversity scores precomputed; selection maximizes diversity; no constraint on individual function quality.
primitives.breakdown_regime: All pairs have δ≈0 (collinear rankings); 𝒫 empty; diversity maximization selects pathological functions with high variance but low relevance.

layer2.mapping: Pair selection ≡ GSI Bayesian model averaging weight w(α,β) ∝ exp(λδ(α,β)); GSE policy π(q) = (α*,β*) where λ tuned via cross-validation on historical click data.
layer2.telemetry: Selection frequency of each pair; downstream nDCG@k of α* vs β*; regret bound vs oracle pair.

primitives.name: Ranking Order Divergence Detection
primitives.verbatim_quote: The plurality of search results are pre-sented in an order according to scores from the first scoring function and are presented in an order according to scores from the second scoring function.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N: number of presented results (dimensionless); r_α(i), r_β(i): ranks under α,β (dimensionless); Δ: mean absolute rank displacement (dimensionless) or binary divergence flag
primitives.assumptions: Same document set presented under both rankings; ranks are 1..N permutations; divergence measured on presented subset.
primitives.breakdown_regime: N=1 (trivial); scoring functions produce identical rankings (Δ=0); presentation layer truncates differently for α vs β.

layer2.mapping: Δ(α,β) ≡ GSI conformal prediction set disagreement measure; GSE state transition trigger: if Δ > τ then invoke human rater or bandit exploration; isomorphic to Spearman footrule distance.
layer2.telemetry: Δ distribution per query class; correlation with user satisfaction metrics; false positive rate of divergence detection.

primitives.name: Query-Classified Scoring Function Selection
primitives.verbatim_quote: BACKGROUND This specification relates to using and evaluating web search scoring functions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: q: query (string); C(q): query class label (categorical); c(f): scoring function class compatibility (categorical); ℱ(q): selected function subset (set of functions)
primitives.assumptions: Query classifier C and function tagger c share same taxonomy 𝒞; classification deterministic; each function tagged with single class.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Classifier C(q) low confidence; taxonomy 𝒞 misaligned with relevance; cold-start queries with no class match.

layer2.mapping: ℱ(q) ≡ GSI prior p(f|q) ∝ exp(⟨φ(q), ψ(f)⟩) where φ,ψ embeddings; GSE context-dependent action space restriction; enables hierarchical Thompson sampling over classes.
layer2.telemetry: Classification accuracy vs human labels; nDCG lift from class-conditioned selection; coverage of ℱ(q) across query volume.

reasoning_traces.think:
The patent defines a dual-ranking evaluation loop: (1) classify query q → class C(q); (2) retrieve candidate scoring functions ℱ(q) tagged with C(q); (3) form pairs 𝒫 ⊂ ℱ(q)×ℱ(q); (4) compute diversity δ(α,β;k) via top-k rank correlation (Kendall-τ complement); (5) select (α*,β*) = argmax δ; (6) present results ranked by α* and β*; (7) measure divergence Δ(α*,β*) via rank displacement; (8) if Δ exceeds threshold or history indicates modification, update scoring functions. Mathematically, δ(α,β;k) = 1 - τ_k(α,β) where τ_k is Kendall-τ on top-k. This is isomorphic to the expected information gain IG(α;β) = H(rank_α) - H(rank_α|rank_β) under Plackett-Luce. The pair selection maximizes discriminative power between ranking hypotheses. Failure modes: (a) δ maximization picks orthogonal but irrelevant functions (high variance, low bias); (b) query classification error propagates to wrong ℱ(q); (c) top-k diversity ignores tail relevance. The framework implements a Bayesian model selection where diversity scores approximate log Bayes factors, and divergence detection triggers model revision.
